description: Delete a task. Requires confirm_title to match the task's current title (hallucinated-id guard). Set with_children:true to delete the ENTIRE subtree (the task plus every nested subtask, regardless of status; for a TaskNotes root this recursively deletes the whole cross-file TaskNotes subtree) — DATA-LOSS: the result's deleted_descendants (inline) and deleted_tasknotes_children (cross-file files) report the blast radius. A plain delete instead promotes the task's direct children to top-level and reports promoted_orphans. Deleting a TaskNote also deletes the checklist items in its body, reported as deleted_checklist_items. Either way, dangling dependsOn refs to deleted tasks, body checklist items included, are stripped (stripped_dependencies) — except a ref another live task still answers to (a second holder of the same id, or a task file with the same name) — and dangling projects: refs to a deleted TaskNotes file are stripped vault-wide (stripped_projects). ALWAYS run a with_children:true cascade delete with dry_run:true FIRST to preview the blast radius without mutating, then repeat without dry_run to commit.

dry_run.description:
When true, PREVIEW the delete without mutating: nothing is removed
from disk, but the result still reports `deleted_descendants` (the
cascade blast radius) and `deleted_tasknotes_children`. ALWAYS
dry-run a `with_children:true` cascade delete FIRST to inspect the
blast radius before deleting for real — a wrong id with a
coincidentally-matching `confirm_title` would otherwise nuke a
whole subtree before you saw what it contained.

with_children.description:
When true, delete the task's ENTIRE inline subtree: the task plus
every recursive inline descendant (regardless of status) and their
description blocks, in one write. DATA-LOSS: this deletes ALL
nested subtasks. The result's `deleted_descendants` reports how
many child tasks were removed so you see the blast radius. For a
TaskNotes root, the ENTIRE cross-file TaskNotes subtree is deleted
recursively (Item #5) — `deleted_tasknotes_children` reports how many
child FILES were removed.

name: delete_task
